findingDecisions.reason: Independent typed-frame and digest recomputation matches every published vector; separator collisions are eliminated and domain/role ambiguity controls are distinct.

The closed local union and original P02/P03/P04 repairs work, but the exact activated universe is self-asserted rather than bound to the named C-2 source, and baseline/waiver precedence is internally contradictory. See R8-P1A-RR-01 and R8-P1A-RR-02.
Independent graph derivation equals all 10 declared refs and exact minima; omission, injection, edge omission, and partial-unit mutations reject.
The eight isolated fixtures replay, but crash reclaim is not identity/fence bound and does not apply pending expiry; a subsequent lease can reuse the fence and repin the object. See R8-P1A-RR-03.
Full purge partitions rederive and malicious cross-project lineage rejects.
The live closed D9 axes and complete ordered termination payload are checked; omission, addition, and type confusion reject.
Direct aliases reject, but an equivalent nested self-sign alias under an unchecked key is accepted, and the live product command still checks retention-tiers.v6.json rather than v7. See R8-P1A-RR-04.
Owned and frozen cross-lane checkers are total over the tested root/nested hostile shapes and both owned mutation harnesses enforce dirty-base and non-applying-mutation guards.

newFindings.title: The proof bundle does not bind its required universe to the named C-2 activation source
newFindings.acceptedCounterexample: Replace every evaluationId and predicateId consistently throughout a positive bundle, update requiredUniverse.memberIds, and independently recompute universe, outcome, waiver, and derivation commitments. The owned evaluation checker accepts the wholly substituted activation universe.
newFindings.architecturalImpact: evaluation-proof.v2 declares C-2 supplies exact activation and Coverage identity, but it carries no content-addressed C-2 activation manifest or equivalent external identity. Internal consistency therefore proves only that a bundle agrees with itself, not that it covers the actual plan-stage activation.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Bind requiredUniverse to a concrete immutable C-2 activation artifact/manifest and independently derive exact sorted member IDs from that binding. Reject coordinated whole-universe substitution even when all local commitments are recomputed.
newFindings.falsifier: A rereview independently substitutes the entire local universe and recomputes every local commitment; validation rejects because the frozen C-2 activation source no longer matches.

newFindings.title: Baseline and waiver prose gives contradictory precedence and the checker chooses one branch silently
newFindings.acceptedCounterexample: Take the local advisory baseline-match vector, add a valid waiver targeting that same current match, add the matching waiver proof object, and recompute all commitments and verdict inputs. Validation accepts an advisory verdict.
newFindings.architecturalImpact: The contract says baseline matches are advisory unless independently waived and also says a waiver suppresses exactly that match. Those rules imply the targeted match no longer produces advisory, while policy-ir-1 as implemented checks the baseline before effective-match suppression and derives advisory. Two conforming readers can derive different verdicts.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Specify one normative precedence order, make prose, policy IR, derivation commitment inputs, positive vectors, and checker agree, and add a baseline-plus-waiver golden and inverse mutation.
newFindings.falsifier: The overlap golden has one unambiguous published verdict and an implementation of the other precedence is rejected.

newFindings.title: Crash reclaim is not identity/fence bound and loses queued expiry before permitting repin
newFindings.acceptedCounterexample: CrashReclaimEventV1 contains only kind, projectId, transactionBoundary, atSequence, and observedOwnerAlive. The same event reclaims two states with different leaseId, ownerId, liveness token, and fencing token. If a pinned ref has pending expiry, reclaim leaves the object AVAILABLE while retaining the queued entry; a later resolve-and-pin can reuse the prior fencing token and repin it.
newFindings.architecturalImpact: A stale or misdirected liveness observation is not scoped to the lease it reclaims, fencing is not monotonic, and crash cleanup differs materially from release cleanup. The fixture-local reducer does not establish durable identity/fencing/expiry semantics under event composition.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Bind reclaim to leaseId, owner/liveness identity, and expected fence; require monotonic fence allocation; define and execute pending-expiry cleanup atomically on reclaim; add composed stale-event, pending-expiry, fence-reuse, and repin fixtures.
newFindings.falsifier: A stale/mismatched reclaim rejects, pending expiry is atomically applied on valid reclaim, and no later grant can reuse an old fence or repin an expired object.

newFindings.title: Authority closure is key-name heuristic and the live product join still targets v6
newFindings.acceptedCounterexample: Insert repairs[0].productDecision = {decisionId: CD-RT-5, outcome: APPROVED, by: architecture-candidate}. Both the retention checker and product checker explicitly pointed at v7 accept it. Separately, the normal product checker is configured to read retention-tiers.v6.json, so its green run does not join the v7 candidate at all.
newFindings.architecturalImpact: Equivalent product self-sign authority can hide below an unchecked alias, while the actual cross-lane command reports green over a stale candidate. Pending-only-CD honesty is therefore not closed under representation or live dependency versioning.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Use a recursively closed top-level and nested schema or deny unknown authority-bearing structures by construction, define authority semantically rather than with selected key names, bind the product checker to v7 (or an explicit reviewed path argument), and retain the hidden-alias regression.
newFindings.falsifier: The hidden productDecision alias is rejected by both checkers, and the normal product command proves from its output or binding that it consumed the exact v7 digest under review.
